# wallix.bastion.connection_policy

Manage connection policies on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.0.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete a connection policy on a WALLIX Bastion.
- A connection policy sets the authentication methods and the protocol options (session, recording, algorithms, ...) of the sessions that use it.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_connection_policy` Terraform resource.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-authentication-methods"></a>**authentication_methods** | `list / elements=str` | Authentication methods allowed by the policy. Order does not matter.<br>Known values are `PASSWORD_VAULT`, `PASSWORD_MAPPING`, `PASSWORD_INTERACTIVE`, `PUBKEY_VAULT`, `PUBKEY_AGENT_FORWARDING` and `KERBEROS_FORWARDING`; which ones are accepted depends on the protocol.<br>When set, replaces all the methods of the policy. Most protocols require at least one. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-connection-policy-name"></a>**connection_policy_name** | `str` / required | Name of the connection policy. Identifies the policy on the Bastion. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-description"></a>**description** | `str` | Description of the policy. |
| <a id="parameter-options"></a>**options** | `dict` | Protocol options, as a dictionary of sections, for example `{"session": {"inactivity_timeout": 600}}`. A JSON string is accepted too.<br>Only the sections and keys given are compared and sent; the Bastion merges them into the current options and fills every other key with its defaults. Key order is irrelevant.<br>Keys cannot be removed, only set to another value. Values are compared with their type, so use the type the Bastion returns (`"1"` and `1` are different). |
| <a id="parameter-protocol"></a>**protocol** | `str` | Protocol of the policy, for example `SSH`, `RDP`, `VNC`, `TELNET`, `RLOGIN`, `RAWTCPIP` or `WEBAPP`. The Bastion validates the value.<br>Required when the policy does not exist yet and [`state=present`](#parameter-state).<br>Cannot be changed after creation; the module fails if it differs. |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | Whether the connection policy should exist.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-type"></a>**type** | `str` | Type of the policy, a variant of [`protocol`](#parameter-protocol) such as `SSH-ccn` or `RDP-ccn` (the Bastion validates the value against the protocol).<br>Defaults to [`protocol`](#parameter-protocol) on creation with API v3.12.<br>Cannot be changed after creation; the module fails if it differs. |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- Do not manage the built-in policies (`SSH`, `RDP`, ...) with this module.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: SSH policy with a 10 minute inactivity timeout
  wallix.bastion.connection_policy:
    connection_policy_name: ssh-strict
    protocol: SSH
    description: SSH with vault credentials only
    authentication_methods: [PASSWORD_VAULT, PUBKEY_VAULT]
    options:
      session:
        inactivity_timeout: 600
      trace:
        log_all_kbd: true

- name: RDP policy refusing unknown server certificates
  wallix.bastion.connection_policy:
    connection_policy_name: rdp-strict
    protocol: RDP
    authentication_methods: [PASSWORD_VAULT]
    options:
      server_cert:
        server_cert_check: "2"

- name: Remove a connection policy
  wallix.bastion.connection_policy:
    connection_policy_name: ssh-strict
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the connection policy already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["options"]` |
| <a id="return-connection-policy"></a>**connection_policy** | `dict` | The connection policy as returned by the Bastion API after the change, including every option section with the Bastion defaults.<br>In check mode, the expected policy. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-connection-policy) |

<a id="sample-connection-policy"></a>

### Sample of `connection_policy`

```yaml
authentication_methods:
- PUBKEY_VAULT
- PASSWORD_VAULT
connection_policy_name: ssh-strict
description: SSH with vault credentials only
id: 1a0f6dbb76cf1460005056b66c8b
is_default: false
options:
  session:
    allow_multi_channels: false
    force_shell_disconnection: false
    inactivity_timeout: 600
    server_keepalive_interval: 0
    server_keepalive_type: none
  trace:
    log_all_kbd: true
    log_group_membership: false
protocol: SSH
type: SSH
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/connectionpolicies/1a0f6dbb76cf1460005056b66c8b
```
